issues.title: vectorElemMinSize floors a zero-dim nested vector at 1 byte, rejecting valid payloads
issues.verdictReason: Verified: unmarshalVector(outer dim=2, inner fixed vector dim=0, []byte{}) decodes to [[] []] on main but errors "2 dimensions do not fit in 0 bytes" on this branch, because vectorElemMinSize (marshal.go:1141-1144) floors a 0-dimension inner vector's true 0-byte size to 1.
issues.scopeReason: The bound and its floor are wholly new code added by this PR and this is a regression it introduces.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: vectorElemMinSize floors a zero-dimension inner vector at 1 byte, but such an element really takes 0 bytes. The bound therefore rejects payloads that base decoded, and the test comment justifying the floor is false.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/tidepoo: vectorElemMinSize floors a zero-dimension inner vector at 1 byte, but such an element really takes 0 bytes. The bound therefore rejects payloads that base decoded, and the test comment justifying the floor is false.

issues.title: unmarshalVector head comment wrongly says every path allocates
issues.verdictReason: The array branch at marshal.go:1078-1081 writes into the caller's existing array via rv.Index(i) and calls neither make nor reflect.MakeSlice; the PR's own test comment at marshal_vector_test.go:649 says "An array allocates nothing", contradicting the new head comment.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new text added by this PR's own commit.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new head comment in unmarshalVector says 'every path below turns it into an allocation (make, reflect.MakeSlice)'. The array path allocates nothing, and the PR's own test comment says so.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/tidepoo: The new head comment in unmarshalVector says 'every path below turns it into an allocation (make, reflect.MakeSlice)'. The array path allocates nothing, and the PR's own test comment says so.

issues.title: Fast-path comment is stale: new bound intercepts non-nil empty payloads first
issues.verdictReason: For data != nil, len(data)==0 and Dimensions>0, the new bound check at marshal.go:998-1003 runs first and rejects with len(data)/elemMin==0 < Dimensions, so the case no longer reaches or 'falls through' the fast-path code the comment describes.
issues.scopeReason: The new bound, placed ahead of the pre-existing comment, is what makes the comment stale.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The pre-existing fast-path comment "nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path" is now stale: a non-nil empty payload with Dimensions>0 is rejected by the new bound before reaching the fast path or the generic path.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/tidepoo: The pre-existing fast-path comment "nil/empty and dim=0 fall through to the generic path" is now stale: a non-nil empty payload with Dimensions>0 is rejected by the new bound before reaching the fast path or the generic path.

However every recent commit on this branch (e.g. 'fix(connectionpool): ...', 'docs(conn): ...') uses the identical conventional-commit style with no trailer, so this is the repo's actual established practice, not something this PR alone deviates from.
issues.scopeReason: The whole branch's commit history already abandoned this CONTRIBUTING.md format; this PR just follows existing, if undocumented, project practice.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Both commit messages break CONTRIBUTING.md's required format. The short description is lowercase with a conventional-commit prefix (`fix(marshal): reject ...`), when it should start with a capital letter, and neither message has the `Patch by <authors>; reviewed by <Reviewers> for #####` trailer.

issues.title: Test doc's "on or above the boundary" claim doesn't fit the null-value subtest
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed by reading unmarshalVector: the bound (marshal.go:998) only runs when data != nil, so for the 'null value' subtest (data: nil) the bound is skipped entirely rather than being met 'on or above' any computed boundary, and the bound is N*elemMin bytes, not 'N bytes' as the doc comment states.
issues.scopeReason: The doc comment and the test it describes are both new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads' doc justifies non-narrowing by 'a vector of N elements is never encoded in fewer than N bytes, so each of these sits on or above the boundary', but the bound enforces N*elemMin bytes, and the 'null value' subtest is not on or above any boundary (the bound is skipped for nil).

issues.title: Commit message's "one byte per element" claim misdescribes the per-type bound
issues.verdictReason: Commit 0276a66 adds vectorElemMinSize with per-type minimums (4 bytes for int/float, 8 for bigint/double, 16 for UUID, etc., marshal.go:1147-1159) in the same commit whose message claims 'every element takes at least one byte on the wire' -- the 1-byte value is only the fallback floor for degenerate (zero/negative-dimension) nested-vector elements, not the general rule the message describes.
issues.scopeReason: The inaccurate description is in this PR's own commit message for the code it is introducing.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: Commit 0276a66's message describes a one-byte-per-element floor that the code does not implement. It also says every element takes at least one byte, which is false for a zero-dimension fixed inner vector.

issues.title: Nested-vector "no Go type" error drops the inner element type and dimensions
issues.verdictReason: Verified: Unmarshal on a wire-decoded vector<vector<float,3>,2> into *any produces 'unmarshal vector: no Go type for element type custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)'. VectorType has no own NewWithError/String, so both are promoted from its embedded NativeType, whose custom field (helpers.go/frame.go construction) is always the bare 'VectorType' prefix with no inner type or dimensions, so %v on info.SubType loses that information.
issues.scopeReason: This error path and its %v formatting are new code added by this PR specifically to report which type the server sent.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: For a nested vector, the new error at marshal.go:1048 prints info.SubType with %v. The inner VectorType that getCassandraLongType builds has custom set to the bare prefix (helpers.go:271), and VectorType has no String method of its own, so the message reads "no Go type for element type custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)". The inner element type and its dimensions are dropped.

issues.verdictReason: Verified: on main, unmarshalVector with data=nil and Dimensions=-3 returns nil (silently leaves dst empty); on this branch it now errors 'negative dimensions -3' because the new check at marshal.go:992-994 runs before the nil-data branch. The PR body (via gh pr view 1) documents only the short/zero-length non-NULL payload behavior change, not this NULL case.

The commit message does not mention either change; only the PR body describes the short-payload case, and neither mentions the NULL case.

issues.title: Nested vector with nonpositive inner dimension defeats the new allocation bound
issues.verdictReason: Verified vectorElemMinSize(subtype) returns 1 whenever the subtype is itself a VectorType with Dimensions <= 0 (the vec.Dimensions > 0 branch is skipped and size floors to 1 at marshal.go:1141-1144), so an outer vector whose element type is a server-declared nested vector with a nonpositive inner dimension bounds Dimensions only by len(data), letting reflect.MakeSlice allocate up to one slice-header-sized element per payload byte (~24x overhead) before the inner vector's own dimension is ever validated -- exactly the unbounded-allocation class of defect this PR otherwise fixes.
issues.scopeReason: vectorElemMinSize and its floor are new code from this PR, and this is a gap in the very protection the PR adds.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: A nested vector with a nonpositive inner dimension still receives the one-byte fallback, so the outer bound can allow one claimed outer element per payload byte and allocate the entire outer slice before the inner decoder rejects the metadata.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-six-pass-batched-2026-10-08/tidepoo: A nested vector with a nonpositive inner dimension still receives the one-byte fallback, so the outer bound can allow one claimed outer element per payload byte and allocate the entire outer slice before the inner decoder rejects the metadata.
